| bp-0004 | NEGATIVE — the reader mirrors /v1/seats faithfully, INCLUDING tombstones once pij-rs sets them. | ph-0001 | BUILD | computational | RUN: adopt a scratch pane, confirm it reaches the reader, kill it, then assert the reader's row for that id matches a direct /v1/seats read at the same moment — including tombstoned_at, whatever its value. The reader must never disagree with the daemon in either direction. | [ ] unchecked | RE-SPECIFIED 2026-09-03, and the original is kept here because the reason matters more than the row. It read 'a closed seat disappears from the reader within 2s'. That is UNMEETABLE: pij-rs does not reap or tombstone a dead seat. Measured — scratch seat pij-semantic-pennyroyal, pane killed, pid confirmed dead by ps, still listed untombstoned as state:'idle' 175s later. Census of the whole roster: 716 of 744 untombstoned paned seats (96%) point at panes that do not exist, and all 716 report 'idle'. Independently reproduced by pij-binding-magpie with a different script, same numbers to the row. An rs row carries no liveness key, so a corpse and a quiet live seat are BYTE-IDENTICAL. This is NOT a defect in the reader: bp-0002 compared 838 seats with zero field mismatches. The criterion was measuring pij-rs's behaviour, not ours. It is re-specified rather than dropped because dropping it would have hidden precisely this finding. KNOWN LIMITATION, tracked as oq-0004: until pij-rs reaps, a chainglass rail on rs shows dead seats as healthy idle ones. chainglass will NOT derive liveness from pid+proc_start — that re-implements pij's contract outside pij and would silently diverge the first time their definition of dead changes. Roadmap question routed to Jordan. METHOD GAP CLOSED BY pij-capitalist-boa, recorded because my control could not have caught it: `tmux list-panes -a` enumerates only the tmux server on the socket you are attached to, so a seat living in a DIFFERENT server (-L name, or another TMUX_TMPDIR) would be invisible and counted dead. My 28-alive control proves the matcher resolves panes in the server it can reach and says nothing about one it cannot. boa measured it instead of caveating it: /tmp/tmux-501 holds 5967 socket entries, but exactly TWO live servers (default, 60 panes; simple-demo, 1 non-pij pane) — 61 live panes total, so exposure is one pane in another project and the 716 stands. boa's incidental finding is the better one: 5967 socket files against 2 live servers is the SAME disease as the seat registry — dead things nothing reaps, and a listing that cannot tell them from live ones. That is an independent instance of this root cause on the same machine, which argues a missing reaper is a habit here rather than one gap in rs. Third symptom, also boa's: a send to a corpse fails with 'pane_in_mode ... expected 0 or 1 — update pij-tmux', which names a tmux capability problem and sends the reader off to upgrade a package. So the gap does not only render wrong, it CORRUPTS THE DIAGNOSTIC PATH. Three symptoms, one root: renders healthy, retries hundreds of times, errors misleadingly. | — | — |
